name: Look At All These
look: Film still of Julie Andrews as Maria, in a dark blue dress with a pale blue apron, spinning with her arms spread wide across a sunny meadow of yellow wildflowers, with snow-capped Alpine peaks behind her.
use: Joyfully shows off having lots of something. The top text says "Look at all these" and the bottom names the thing, often something bad like bills or unread emails for irony.
slots: the thing there's a lot of (bottom text)
describe: woman spinning in a field of flowers with mountains behind her
julie andrews twirling with her arms out on a hill
sound of music nun spinning on an alpine meadow
happy lady in a blue dress dancing in the mountains
girl twirling in a flower meadow singing the hills are alive
origin: Julie Andrews as Maria singing the title song in the opening scene of The Sound of Music (1965).
